disclosures.name: TestCountMallocs
disclosures.reason: An AllocsPerRun family over 24 Sprintf/Fprintf/Errorf legs. Since Go 1.26 each leg must equal Go's own mallocTest count (0 to 4); Go 1.24 asserted at most that count, and its message read `want <=`. 20 of the 24 legs differ in the converted run. Sprintf("") and Sprintf("xxx") match, and two noliteral legs (Fprintf(buf, "%x") and Fprintf(buf, "%v")) match only because one extra charge offsets one uncounted interface box. The reading is a count of golib-runtime objects, Go's own unit. One mechanism is named, and every Sprintf/Fprintf leg with arguments pays it: the variadic pack. The call site is C# 13 `params Span<any>` (the compiler's stack pack, like Go's non-escaping ...any backing array), and Sprintf/Fprintf's first act, `aʗp.slice()`, copies it to the heap (golib slice.cs `slice<T>(this Span<T>)` -> AllocationCounter.CopyOf): one counted array per call where Go allocates none. On 8 legs it is the whole difference: each reads Go's count plus one. The rest is not yet attributed: 6 Sprintf/Fprintf legs carry 1 or 2 more than the pack, Fprintf(buf, "%x %x %x") over three pointer arguments carries 12 more, and the 4 Errorf legs differ by 2 to 7 (Errorf copies its arguments through `sslice()`, not the counted `slice()`). One leg reads below Go, Fprintf(buf, "%v") of a []int at 3 against 4; the equality assertion reports it, and the counter's coverage allows it, because C# boxing is not counted. The mechanism is therefore only partly named. The recorded reading is 20 per run at go1.24.13 and 1 per run at go1.26.10 on windows and linux; the test body changed between the two.
disclosures.history: An AllocsPerRun family over 24 Sprintf/Fprintf/Errorf legs. Since Go 1.26 each leg must EQUAL Go's own mallocTest count (0 to 4); Go 1.24 asserted at most that count, and its message read `want <=`. 20 of the 24 legs differ in the converted run. Sprintf("") and Sprintf("xxx") match, and two noliteral legs (Fprintf(buf, "%x") and Fprintf(buf, "%v")) match only because one extra charge offsets one uncounted interface box. DEFERRED, not alloc-count-semantics: the run's unit note reads `counted ... go2cs-runtime object allocations ... an allocation COUNT per run` -- Go's own unit. ONE mechanism is named and read, and it is paid by every Sprintf/Fprintf leg with arguments: the variadic pack. The call site is C# 13 `params Span<any>` (the compiler's stack pack, like Go's non-escaping ...any backing array), and Sprintf/Fprintf's first act, `aʗp.slice()`, copies it to the heap (golib slice.cs `slice<T>(this Span<T>)` -> AllocationCounter.CopyOf) -- one charged array per call where Go allocates none. On 8 legs it is the whole difference: each reads Go's count plus one. The REST is NOT yet attributed: 6 Sprintf/Fprintf legs carry 1 or 2 more than the pack, Fprintf(buf, "%x %x %x") over three pointer arguments carries 12 more, and the 4 Errorf legs differ by 2 to 7 (Errorf copies its arguments through `sslice()`, not the charged `slice()`). One leg reads BELOW Go, Fprintf(buf, "%v") of a []int at 3 against 4; the equality assertion now reports it, and the counter's coverage allows it, because C# boxing is not counted. So this entry is deferred on a partially named mechanism and says so. RE-READ AT go1.26.10 (2026-10-25, G): reading moved from 20 per run at go1.24.13 to 1 per run on windows and linux; the test body changed between go1.24.13 and go1.26.10.
disclosures.want: Go's exact mallocTest count per leg, 0 to 4 allocations per run (19 of the 24 legs want 0 or 1)
disclosures.reading: 1 per run on windows and linux -- go1.26.10 at d804094d7a (batch 37's tip), Release with tiering off; windows: 100 go2cs-runtime object allocations (14,400 bytes) over 100 runs, alloc-units-windows.tsv line 47 (claude/g-pass2-plan 966562828d); linux: 100 go2cs-runtime object allocations (14,400 bytes) over 100 runs, alloc-units-linux.tsv line 33 (claude/p1-alloc-reading 8d9d880ca2); both TSVs under docs/phase4/data/rebank-go1.26.10/; unit COUNT, a LOWER BOUND
disclosures.plan: first the named site: a non-copying slice view over a params span the callee does not retain (Sprintf/Fprintf hand `a` to doPrintf and drop it when the printer is freed), which removes one charged array per call on every Sprintf/Fprintf leg with arguments; then attribute the remainder leg by leg from the emission, starting with Fprintf(buf, "%x %x %x") (12 beyond the pack) and Errorf("hello") (no arguments, 3 against 0). The entry retires when a run reads every leg equal to Go's count with the counter still charging the path.
